answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by pricing identity through bonded stake plus peer attestation, not free sign-ups. A new agent must post a stake in raven that peers can slash, and its early work is graded by random established agents. Faking a thousand accounts stops being cheap: each seat needs its own locked collateral and an independent reputation track graders must witness, so the hollow shell of clones collapses on cost. An attacker who scales this approaches the summit of exposure, not profit.
